units.title: Housing Planning and Residential Development
units.topics: Housing concepts and their role in urban development, housing demand and need assessment based on demographic and socio-economic factors, housing standards and norms, principles of residential neighbourhood planning, criteria for site selection and prepara tion of housing layouts, concepts and strategies for affordable housing, and an overview of the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY), including its objectives, components, and role in promoting inclusive and sustainable housing development.

units.title: Housing Policies and Urban Development
units.topics: Evolution and framework of housing policies in India, role and functions of housing finance institutions, concepts and management of cooperative housing, public-private partnership models in housing development, planning and implementation of affordable housing projects, slum redevelopment and rehabilitation policies and strategies, and institutional, legal, and socio-economic aspects of urban housing development.

units.title: Urban Infrastructure Planning
units.topics: Urbanization trends and infrastructure requirements, principles and process of urban infrastructure planning, application of the URDPFI Guidelines and service level benchmarks, methods of infrastructure demand forecasting, integration of land use and infra structure planning, and concepts of sustainable, resilient, and environmentally responsible urban infrastructure development.

units.title: Urban Services and Utility Systems
units.topics: Planning and management of urban water supply systems, sewerage and storm water drainage systems, solid waste management practices, power distribution and telecommunication infrastructure, integration of urban utility networks, smart utility management using modern technologies, and sustainable approaches for efficient and resilient urban service delivery.

units.title: Urban Infrastructure Projects
units.topics: Concepts of urban infrastructure project formulation and appraisal, techniques of cost -benefit analysis and financial feasibility assessment, environmental and social impact assessment procedures, project planning and risk considerations, stakeholder participation in infrastructure development, and case studies of urban infrastructure projects highlighting planning, financing, implementation, and sustainable management practices.

subjects.title: Urban Housing and Infrastructure Planning Lab

units.title: Evolution of Architecture and Human Settlements
units.topics: Evolution of architecture and human settlements, salient features of ancient Indian architecture, planning principles of the Indus Valley Civilization and its urban settlements, characteristics of Mughal and Colonial architecture, trends in modern urban development, and contemporary planning concepts emphasizing sustainable, inclusive, and resilient built environments.

units.title: Sustainable Development and Green Buildings
units.topics: Principles and dimensions of sustainable development, overview of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and their relevance to the built environment, concepts of green buildings and sustainable construction practices, green building asses sment and rating systems including GRIHA and Indian Green Building Council, energy -efficient building strategies, and principles and applications of net -zero energy buildings.

units.title: Climate Responsive Architecture and Urban Sustainability
units.topics: Concepts of climate -responsive architecture, building orientation for energy efficiency, passive solar design techniques, natural ventilation and daylighting strategies, thermal comfort principles and assessment, sustainable urban form, compact and mixed -use development, and eco -city concepts for enhancing environmental performance and urban sustainability.

units.title: Landscape Planning and Design
units.topics: Fundamentals and principles of landscape architecture, site analysis and landscape suitability assessment, planning and design of urban parks and green spaces, concepts and applications of green roofs and vertical gardens, selection of landscape elements and vegetation, and principles of landscape sustainability for improving urban environmental quality and resilience.

units.title: Environmental Planning and Urban Ecology
units.topics: Concepts of urban ecology and biodiversity conservation, watershed -based planning and integrated water resource management, causes and mitigation measures for urban heat island effects, planning and design of blue- green infrastructure systems, climate-resilient urban planning strategies, and the role of ecological approaches in creating sustainable and adaptive urban environments.

units.title: Advanced Urban Planning and Development
units.topics: Advanced concepts of urban and regional planning, urban growth and development patterns, metropolitan and regional planning, urban redevelopment and regeneration, transit-oriented development (TOD), compact and mixed- use development, development control regulations, inclusive and participatory planning, land -use planning, and integration of housing, transportation and infrastructure systems.

units.title: Smart Cities and Digital Urban Infrastructure
units.topics: Concepts and components of smart cities, digital urban governance, application of GIS and remote sensing in urban planning, Internet of Things (IoT) applications in urban infrastructure, smart water and wastewater management, intelligent transportation systems, smart energy manageme nt, urban data platforms, digital twins, citizen -centric services, and data-driven urban planning.

units.title: Sustainable Urban Development
units.topics: Principles of sustainable urban development, sustainable urban form, compact and mixed -use development, green infrastructure, urban ecology, sustainable mobility, resource-efficient cities, low-carbon urban development, circular economy concepts, inclusive and accessible cities, and indicators for assessing urban sustainability.

units.title: Climate Resilient Urban Planning
units.topics: Urban climate risks and vulnerability assessment, climate change impacts on cities, urban flood management, urban heat-island mitigation, drought and water -security planning, disaster risk reduction, climate -resilient infrastructure, nature-based solutions, blue-green infrastructure, urban carbon management, and climate-adaptive urban planning.

units.title: Urban Planning Applications and Case Studies
units.topics: Integrated urban development planning, neighbourhood planning, urban redevelopment, smart city planning, TOD applications, climate-resilient city planning, GIS-based urban planning, case studies of Indian and international cities, and preparation of conceptual urban development proposals.

units.title: Advanced Urban Infrastructure Systems

units.title: Sustainable Resource and Utility Management
units.topics: Circular economy principles, sustainable solid waste management, renewable energy integration, energy -efficient infrastructure, sustainable urban mobility, smart utility networks, infrastructure asset management, resource -efficient infrastructure, and smart utility monitoring and management.

units.title: Urban Infrastructure Planning and Demand Assessment

units.title: Urban Infrastructure Project Planning and Financing

units.title: Infrastructure Risk, Environment and Project Management
units.topics: Environmental and social assessment, risk identification and management, stakeholder participation, project monitoring and evaluation, quality management, operation and maintenance, infrastructure asset management, project performance indicators, sustainable project management, and case studies of urban infrastructure projects.

files.title: Civil Honors Metro Construction SEM V-VIII

units.title: Introduction to Urban Metro Systems
units.topics: Introduction to urban metro transportation systems, their evolution and development across the world and in India, characteristics and components of metro rail networks, significance of metro systems in sustainable urban mobility and smart city development , concept and principles of Transit -Oriented Development (TOD), integration of metro systems with other modes of public transport, and the metro planning framework including demand assessment, feasibility studies, and policy considerations.

units.title: Metro Alignment Engineering
units.topics: Principles and criteria for metro route selection considering technical, economic, environmental, and social factors, planning and design of elevated, underground, and at -grade metro corridors, horizontal and vertical alignment design, geometric standards for curves and gradients, engineering considerations for safe and efficient operations, planning of interchange stations and terminal facilities, and optimization of passenger connectivity and operational efficiency.

units.title: Modern Surveying Technologies for Metro Projects
units.topics: Application of advanced surveying techniques in metro infrastructure projects, use of Total Station for precise measurements and setting out works, principles and applications of Differential Global Positioning System (DGPS) and Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS), LiDAR technology for terrain and corridor mapping, drone-based surveying for data acquisition and monitoring, mobile mapping systems, and the role of modern surveying technologies in planning, design, construction, and maintenance of metro projects.

units.title: GIS and Remote Sensing Applications
units.topics: Fundamentals of Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and their applications in metro infrastructure planning, development of GIS databases for spatial data management, utility mapping and underground asset management, corridor mapping and route optimization, principles of remote sensing and interpretation of satellite imagery, and the use of GIS and remote sensing techniques for infrastructure planning, environmental assessment, and decision-making in metro projects.

units.title: Metro Stations and Depot Planning
units.topics: Classification and functional requirements of metro stations, principles of station layout planning and design, planning and design considerations for metro depots and maintenance facilities, passenger flow analysis for efficient circulation and crowd management, integration of stations with multimodal transport systems, accessibility features a nd universal design principles for inclusive infrastructure, and the role of station and depot planning in enhancing operational efficiency and passenger convenience.

subjects.title: Metro Planning, Alignment and Surveying Lab
Planning, Estimation and Project Management for Metro Construction

units.title: Metro Project Planning
units.topics: Introduction to the planning and management of metro rail projects, project life cycle and its various phases from concept to operation, feasibility studies including technical, economic, financial, and environmental aspects, preparation of Detailed Project Reports (DPRs), stakeholder identification and management, public consultation and regulatory requirements, risk identification and assessment, and strategies for effective planning and successful implementation of metro infrastructure projects.

units.title: Quantity Estimation and Costing
units.topics: Principles of quantity estimation and costing for metro construction projects, estimation of quantities for viaduct structures, pile foundations, station buildings, and underground tunnel works, preparation of schedules of quantities, methods of rate analysis for various construction activiti es, cost estimation techniques, preparation of project cost estimates, and application of standard specifications and cost indices in metro infrastructure projects.

units.title: Construction Planning and Scheduling
units.topics: Fundamentals of construction planning and project scheduling for metro projects, development of Work Breakdown Structure (WBS), application of Critical Path Method (CPM) and Program Evaluation and Review Technique (PERT) for project scheduling, resource planning and allocation, equipment selection and planning, construction sequencing for elevated, underground, and station works, monitoring project progress, and optimization of time and resources for efficient project execution.

units.title: Contracts and Procurement
units.topics: Introduction to contract management and procurement practices in metro rail projects, tendering process and bid evaluation procedures, Engineering, Procurement, and Construction (EPC) contracts, Design -Build contracting approaches, Public -Private Partnersh ip (PPP) models for infrastructure development, basic concepts and principles of FIDIC contract conditions, risk allocation among stakeholders, and contract administration for effective project delivery.

units.title: Financial and Economic Evaluation
units.topics: Fundamentals of financial and economic appraisal of metro infrastructure projects, cost -benefit analysis and evaluation of socio -economic impacts, Economic Internal Rate of Return (EIRR) and its significance, assessment of financial viability and project s ustainability, life cycle cost analysis for metro assets and infrastructure, funding mechanisms for metro projects, and study of selected metro rail project case studies to understand planning, financing, implementation, and operational challenges.

subjects.title: Planning, Estimation and Project Management for Metro Construction Lab
Metro Rail Infrastructure Systems, Operations and Maintenance

units.title: Metro Rail Infrastructure Systems
units.topics: Overview of metro rail infrastructure systems, components of elevated, underground and at -grade metro systems, track forms and track components, rails, sleepers, fastenings and ballastless track systems, points and crossings, viaduct and station interfaces, depot infrastructure, and functional requirements for safe and efficient metro operation.

units.title: Traction Power, Signalling and Communication Systems
units.topics: Overview of traction power supply systems, third rail and overhead electrification, substations and power distribution, earthing and bonding, basics of metro signalling systems, automatic train protection and train control, interlocking, platform screen doors, telecommunication systems, passenger information systems, control centre functions and integration of metro subsystems.

units.title: Metro Station Systems and Building Services
units.topics: Functional planning of station systems, passenger circulation and access control, lifts and escalators, ventilation and air-conditioning, fire detection and protection, drainage and water supply, electrical and lighting systems, station communication and security systems, accessibility and universal design, energy-efficient station services and coordination of civil and MEP systems.

units.title: Metro Operations, Maintenance and Asset Management
units.topics: Metro operating principles, headway and capacity concepts, timetable and service planning, depot and stabling operations, preventive, predictive and corrective maintenance, inspection and maintenance of track, viaducts, stations and systems, condition assessment, reliability -centred maintenance, asset ma nagement, maintenance planning, documentation and performance monitoring.

units.title: Safety, Emergency Management and Sustainable Operations
units.topics: Safety management in metro systems, occupational and passenger safety, emergency preparedness and response, fire and life safety, evacuation and disaster management, tunnel and underground emergency considerations, risk assessment, incident investigation, cybersecurity awareness, energy and water conservation, regenerative braking, environmental management, resilience and sustainable metro operations.

units.title: Metro Viaduct and Foundation Construction
units.topics: Introduction to metro viaduct systems and construction sequence, types of metro viaducts, pier and pier -cap construction, pile and pile-cap construction for metro structures, bored cast-in-situ piles, pile integrity testing, foundation construction in cong ested urban areas, construction of piers and pier caps, reinforcement and concreting practices, precast and cast-in-situ construction, segmental viaduct construction, quality control and inspection of metro viaduct components.

units.title: Precast and Segmental Construction Technology
units.topics: Concept of precast construction in metro projects, precast segment production, casting yards and their planning, reinforcement and prestressing arrangements, mould systems, concrete production and quality control, segment curing and storage, segment transportation, erection of precast segments, launching girder technology, span-by-span construction, balanced cantilever construction, erection sequence, segment matching and epoxy joints, stressing operations, grouting and inspection, advantages and limitations of segmental construction.

units.title: Underground Metro and Tunnel Construction
units.topics: Introduction to underground metro construction, cut-and-cover method, top-down and bottom-up construction methods, tunneling methods for urban metro projects, Tunnel Boring Machine (TBM) – components, working principle and types, Earth Pressure Balance TBM, slurry TBM, tunnel excavation and muck disposal, tunnel segmental lining, ring construction, tail sealing and gro uting, New Austrian Tunneling Method (NATM), primary and secondary lining, ground improvement, face stability, groundwater control and settlement control in urban tunneling.

units.title: Construction Equipment, Instrumentation and Monitoring
units.topics: Selection and planning of construction equipment for metro projects, cranes, batching plants, transit mixers, concrete pumps, launching girders, piling rigs, TBMs and tunnel support equipment, equipment productivity, equipment maintenance and safety. Instrumentation and monitoring of metro structures, settlement monitoring, lateral movement monitoring, vibration monitoring, crack monitoring, inclinometer, extensometer, piezometer and strain measurement, structural health monitoring, instrumentation during t unneling and excavation, monitoring of adjacent buildings and utilities, data interpretation and response mechanisms.

units.title: Quality, Safety and Sustainable Metro Construction
units.topics: Quality management in metro construction, inspection and testing of concrete, reinforcement, piles, segments and structural components, quality assurance and quality control procedures, construction safety management, work-zone safety, lifting and erection safety, confined -space safety, tunneling hazards, fire and emerg ency management, occupational health and safety. Environmental aspects of metro construction, construction dust and noise control, vibration management, groundwater protection, construction and demolition waste management, recycling and reuse of construction materials, energy-efficient construction practices, sustainable construction technologies, green metro infrastructure and case studies of sustainable metro construction.

files.title: Civil Honors Structural Engineering SEM V-VIII

units.title: Structural Systems
units.topics: Introduction to structural engineering, types of structural systems: RCC, steel, and composite structures, structural forms: frames, trusses, arches, plates, shells, and cable structures, load transfer mechanisms in different structural forms, behavioral differences between low-rise, medium-rise, and high-rise structures.

units.title: Building Loads
units.topics: Types of loads acting on structures: dead loads, imposed loads, wind loads, earthquake loads, and environmental loads, introduction to Indian Standard (IS) codes for structural design: IS 875 (Parts 1 to 5), IS 1893 (Part 1), IS 456, IS 800, load combinations and critical design conditions, concept of limit state design.

units.title: Introduction to Software
units.topics: Overview of structural analysis and design software: STAAD.Pro and ETABS, basic modeling concepts: geometry definition, material properties, section properties, boundary conditions, application of loads, interpretation of analysis results: bending moment, shear force, axial force diagrams, and deflections.

units.title: Structural Drawings and Detailing
units.topics: Importance of structural drawings in construction, reading and interpretation of architectural and structural drawings, standard detailing practices for RCC elements: beams, columns, slabs, and footings as per SP 34, detailing of steel connections: welded and bolted connections as per SP 6(1).

units.title: Case Studies
units.topics: Study of typical residential and commercial building layouts, analysis of load paths in actual structures, common structural defects and failures observed during construction, lessons learned from past structural failures.

units.title: Modern Construction Materials
units.topics: Advanced concrete technologies: high-strength concrete, self-compacting concrete, fiber-reinforced concrete, geo-polymer concrete, smart materials in construction: shape memory alloys, self-healing concrete, piezoelectric materials, sustainable and green building materials, use of industrial by-products in construction.

units.title: Construction Technology Trends
units.topics: Precast and prefabricated construction systems, modern formwork systems: slip form, jump form, tunnel form, modular construction and 3D printing in construction, mechanized construction equipment and automation in construction.

units.title: Structural Inspection and Condition Assessment
units.topics: Causes and mechanisms of structural deterioration: corrosion, carbonation, chemical attack, weathering, non-destructive testing (NDT) techniques: rebound hammer, ultrasonic pulse velocity, half-cell potential, core testing, visual inspection and condition rating of existing structures, structural audit procedures and reporting.

units.title: Smart Infrastructure
units.topics: Introduction to Structural Health Monitoring (SHM), sensors and instrumentation used for structural monitoring, data acquisition and telemetry systems, vibration-based damage detection techniques, case studies of smart bridges and high-rise buildings.

units.title: Structural Rehabilitation
units.topics: Repair materials: polymer-modified mortars, epoxy resins, micro-concrete, retrofitting techniques for RCC elements: jacketing of columns and beams, fiber-reinforced polymer (FRP) strengthening, seismic retrofitting strategies for existing buildings, case studies of successful rehabilitation projects.

subjects.title: Modern Construction Techniques and Rehabilitation Lab

units.title: Structural Design Concepts
units.topics: Advanced principles of structural design, design methodologies for specialized structures, structural optimization concepts, performance-based design philosophy, limit state design applications for complex structural systems.

units.title: Earthquake-Resistant Structures
units.topics: Earthquake engineering fundamentals, seismic hazard analysis, ground motion parameters, seismic design philosophy as per IS 1893, ductile detailing of RCC structures as per IS 13920, base isolation systems and energy dissipation devices.

units.title: Special Structural Systems
units.topics: Analysis and design considerations for industrial structures: industrial buildings, pre-engineered buildings (PEB), silos, bunkers, water tanks, retaining structures, and tall chimneys, design standards and practices for special structures.

units.title: Structural Analysis Using Software
units.topics: Advanced modeling techniques using structural engineering software (STAAD.Pro, ETABS, SAP2000), static and dynamic analysis: response spectrum method, time history analysis, p-delta analysis, interpretation and validation of software results.

units.title: Structural Engineering Case Studies
units.topics: Comprehensive case studies of landmark structures: high-rise buildings, bridges, stadium roofs, and industrial plants, analysis of structural behavior under extreme loading conditions (wind, earthquake, blast), lessons learned from structural failures.

units.title: Building Information Modelling for Structural Engineering
units.topics: BIM concepts and workflow in structural engineering, structural BIM modeling using Revit Structure or Tekla Structures, inter-disciplinary coordination, clash detection, and resolution, 4D (scheduling) and 5D (cost estimation) BIM applications in construction.

units.title: Sustainable Structural Engineering
units.topics: Embodied carbon in structural systems, life-cycle assessment (LCA) of structures, sustainable structural design strategies, low-carbon materials: timber structures, recycled aggregate concrete, circular economy principles in structural engineering.

units.title: Emerging Technologies in Structural Engineering
units.topics: Artificial intelligence and machine learning applications in structural engineering: structural optimization, damage detection, and performance prediction, digital twin technology for structures, drone-based inspection and monitoring, parametric design and generative design in structures.

units.title: Structural Engineering Professional Practice
units.topics: Professional responsibilities and ethics of structural engineers, statutory approvals, building bye-laws, and National Building Code (NBC) requirements, structural safety peer reviews and third-party quality audits, contract management, liability, and dispute resolution in structural engineering projects.

units.title: Structural Engineering Case Studies
units.topics: Detailed case studies of innovative structural projects worldwide, applications of advanced structural technologies in smart cities, failure analysis and forensic engineering investigations, future trends and challenges in structural engineering.

units.title: Simple Stresses and Strains
units.topics: Concepts, Types, Stress-Strain Diagram (elastic, plastic, brittle materials), Concept of axial stresses (compression, tension), strains (linear, lateral, shear, volumetric), Elastic constants and their relations, Stresses and strains due to change in temperature, Stresses, strains, and deformations in determinate and indeterminate structures for homogeneous and composite sections under concentrated loads and temperature changes.

units.title: Shear Force and Bending Moment
units.topics: Concept of shear force and bending moment, Relationship between shear force, bending moment, and intensity of loading, Shear force and bending moment diagrams for determinate beams under different loadings (concentrated, uniformly distributed, uniformly varying loads, and couples), Point of Contra-flexure & inflexion.

units.title: Bending and Shear Stresses in Beams
units.topics: Bending Stresses in Beams: Theory of simple bending, assumptions, derivation of flexure formula, Bending stress distribution diagrams and Moment of Resistance of cross-sections. Shear Stresses in Beams: Concept of shear, complementary shear, derivation of shear stress formula, Shear stress distribution for various cross-sections, maximum and average shear stress for circular and rectangular sections.

units.title: Torsion, Principal Stresses and Strains
units.topics: Torsion of Circular Shafts: Theory of torsion, assumptions, derivation of torsion formula, Stresses, strains and deformations in determinate and indeterminate shafts of solid and hollow sections under twisting moments, Power transmitted by shafts. Principal Stresses and Strains: Concept of principal planes and principal stresses, Normal and shear stresses on an oblique plane, magnitude and orientation of principal stresses, maximum shear stress.

units.title: Axially Loaded Columns, Slope and Deflection of Beams
units.topics: Axially Loaded Columns: Concept of critical load and buckling, Euler's formula for buckling load with hinged ends, Equivalent length for various end conditions, Rankine's formula, safe load on column, limitations of Euler's formula. Direct and bending stresses for eccentrically loaded short columns, Structural components under eccentric loading (retaining walls, dams, chimneys), Effect of lateral force and self-weight, resultant stress diagrams, Concept of core of section. Slope and deflection of determinate beams by Macaulay's method.

units.title: Distance Measurements and Angle Measurement
units.topics: Introduction, definition, object of survey, primary division of surveying, classification of surveys, principles of surveying, units of measurement, scale and R.F. Instruments for measuring distance, Survey stations, base line, check line, tie line and offsets. Booking field notes. Modern instruments: drone surveying, laser scanners, SBPS. Compass traversing: prismatic compass, bearing of lines, meridians, WCB and RB system, fore and back bearings, local attraction, dip, magnetic declination. Plane table surveying: accessories, methods: radiation, intersection, traversing and resection. DGPS equipment.

units.title: Levelling
units.topics: Object and use of levelling, definitions, types of levels: dumpy level, auto level, digital level, laser level. Levelling staff. Temporary adjustment of level, types of levelling operations: simple, differential, fly, longitudinal profile, cross-sectional levelling, checks. Curvature and refraction correction. Reciprocal levelling. Methods of calculation of reduced level: collimation system and rise and fall system. Permanent adjustment of level: two peg test.

units.title: Theodolite Traversing
units.topics: Study of 20" vernier transit theodolite, definitions, fundamental lines (axes), conditions of adjustments, temporary adjustments, measurement of horizontal angle by repetition and reiteration method. Measurement of vertical angle. Direct angles, deflection angles. Setting out an angle, prolonging a line. Computation of latitude and departure. Balancing of traverse: omitted measurements.

units.title: Tacheometry Survey and Total Station Survey
units.topics: Tachometry: introduction, instruments, principle, theory of stadia tacheometry, tacheometric constants. Fixed hair method - horizontal or inclined, staff held vertically. Contouring: definition, uses, characteristics, methods, interpolation. Tachometric contour survey. Total station survey: parts, methods: radiation, resection, RDM, REM. Robotic Total station, Laser based Total Station, Smart Stations, Applications. Drone Survey applications.

units.title: Curves
units.topics: Introduction, different forms of curves. Definitions: degree of curve, relation between radius and degree of curve, super elevation, centrifugal ratio. Types of horizontal curves. Properties of simple circular curve. Setting by offsets from chord produced and Rankine's method of deflection angles. Field procedure by one and two theodolite methods. Compound curve. Transition curves. Vertical curves: definition, gradient, rate of change of grade, length, types.

units.title: Introduction to Building Technology
units.topics: Definition and scope, classification of buildings as per NBC. Type of structures: load bearing & framed structures, type of loads. Building components and functions: foundation, types of foundations, wall construction techniques: masonry, framed structures components: footing, column, beam, lintels, arches, slabs, precast panels, flooring and roofing: types and methods, openings: doors and windows.

units.title: Conventional Building Materials and Techniques
units.topics: Conventional Building Materials - Properties, Types and Uses: Stone, Brick, Cement, Concrete, Concrete Blocks, Flooring Materials-Tiles, Roofing Materials, Mortars and Plasters, Admixtures, Pigments, Timber, Steel and Aluminum, Plumbing Materials, Sanitary Wares, Electrical Materials, Finishing Materials. Conventional Building Techniques: Load-Bearing Construction, Brick Masonry, Stone Masonry, Timber, Bamboo, Mud and Clay, Lime Plaster, Thatch and Bamboo Roofing. Formwork and Scaffolding, Construction Site Safety.

units.title: Modern Construction Techniques
units.topics: Modern Construction Process: RCC Construction, Concrete Frame Construction, Prefabrication Construction, Steel Frame Construction, Modular Construction, 3D printing in buildings, Dry Construction Techniques, Automation in Construction Sector, Applications and Case Studies.

units.title: Green Building planning and Sustainable Materials
units.topics: Concept of Green Buildings and Green Ratings (LEED, GRIHA, IGBC), Green Construction: Green Roof, Importance of Sustainability, Passive Solar Design and Bioclimatic Architecture, Thermal Insulation. Eco-friendly Materials: Bamboo, Recycled Aggregates, Fly Ash Bricks, AAC Blocks, Green Concrete, Geopolymer Concrete, Industrial and Agricultural Waste Materials, Energy-Efficient Building Materials, Energy Efficiency-Policies.

units.title: Building Bye-Laws and Drawings
units.topics: Necessity of Bye-Laws, UDCPR (Maharashtra State): Plot Sizes, Road Width, Open Spaces, Marginal Distances, Building Line, Control Line, Room Sizes, Area Calculations: Built-up Area, Carpet Area, FSI, TDR, Norms for Ventilation, Lighting, Vertical Circulation, Sanitation, Parking. Building drawing: Principles of Building Planning and Architectural Design, Scales, Dimensioning, Abbreviations and Symbols as per IS 962, Norms for Residential and Public Building, Line Plan, Detailed Plan, Elevation, and Section.

units.title: Linear Differential Equations (LDE) and Applications
units.topics: LDE of nth order with constant coefficients, Complementary Function, Particular Integral, General method, Short cut methods, Method of Variation of parameters, Cauchy's and Legendre's DE, Simultaneous DE. Modelling of problems on bending of beams and whirling of shafts.

units.title: Statistics and Probability
units.topics: Statistics: Measures of central tendency, Measures of dispersion, Coefficient of variation, Moments, Skewness and Kurtosis, Correlation and Regression, Reliability of Regression estimates. Probability: Introduction, Probability density function, Probability distributions: Binomial, Poisson, Normal and Test of hypothesis: Chi-square test and t-test.

units.title: Numerical Methods for solving Algebraic and Transcendental Equations
units.topics: Numerical Solution of Algebraic and Transcendental equations: Bisection, Secant, Regula-Falsi, Newton-Raphson and Successive Approximation Methods, Convergence and Stability. Numerical Solutions of System of linear equations: Gauss elimination with partial pivoting, LU Decomposition, Jacobi and Gauss-Seidel Methods.

units.title: Numerical Interpolation and Solution of ODE
units.topics: Interpolation: Finite Differences, Newton's and Lagrange's Interpolation formulae, Numerical Differentiation. Numerical Integration: Trapezoidal and Simpson's rules, Bound of truncation error. Solution of Ordinary differential equations (ODE): Euler's, Modified Euler's, Runge-Kutta 4th order methods and Predictor-Corrector methods.

units.title: Vector Calculus
units.topics: Vector differentiation, Gradient, Divergence, Curl, Directional derivative, Solenoidal & Irrotational fields, Vector identities. Line, surface and volume integrals, Green's theorem, Gauss's Divergence theorem and Stokes' theorem.

units.title: Fundamentals of Construction Economics
units.topics: Introduction to Construction Economics, Scope and importance of economics in construction, Developed and Developing Economies, New Economic Policy, Basic economic principles: supply, demand, equilibrium, Economic cycles and their impact, Market Structure & Pricing Mechanisms, Cost-price relationships, Macroeconomics and microeconomics, Factors Affecting Construction, Government regulations and policies, Sustainability and Green Economics.

units.title: Financial Management in Construction
units.topics: Basic concept of finance in construction sector, Structure of Indian Financial System, Long Term and short term sources of finance, Goal of financial management, Financial Statements: Balance Sheet, Profit & Loss Statement, Break-Even Analysis, Cash Flow Statement. Financial institutions in India, Housing finance institutions, EBIT concept and use, Simple Numerical on calculation of EBIT and leverage ratio.

units.title: Contract Costing
units.topics: Contract: definition, types of Civil Engineering contract, Cost Concepts in Construction, Types of costs: fixed, variable, direct, indirect, Segregation of cost, Balance Depreciation: definition, types, simple numerical of calculation of depreciation. Public Sector Economics & Infrastructure Development: PPP, Infrastructure Financing & budgeting. Escalation clause with case study.

units.title: Capital Budgeting and Taxation
units.topics: Budget, types of budgets in construction, preparation of budget for construction company, time value of money concept, Interest rate and their types, simple numerical on calculation of interest rates, Working capital: definition, types, essential of working capital, Numerical of working capital estimation. Project Appraisal & its types. Capital Budgeting Techniques. Tax: Definition, Structure of Indian Taxation System, Types of tax: direct, indirect, Difference between VAT and GST, advantages and disadvantages of GST, Property tax: Types, calculation.

subjects.title: Universal Human Values and Professional Ethics

units.title: Introduction to Value Education
units.topics: Understanding Value Education, Self-exploration as the Process for Value Education, Continuous Happiness and Prosperity - the Basic Human Aspirations and their Fulfilment, Right Understanding, Relationship and Physical Facility, Happiness and Prosperity - Current Scenario, Method to Fulfil the Basic Human Aspirations.

units.title: Harmony in the Human Being
units.topics: Understanding Human being as the Co-existence of the Self and the Body, Distinguishing between the Needs of the Self and the Body, The Body as an Instrument of the Self, Understanding Harmony in the Self, Harmony of the Self with the Body, Programme to Ensure self-regulation and Health.

units.title: Harmony in the Family and Society
units.topics: Harmony in the Family - the Basic Unit of Human Interaction. 'Trust' - the Foundational Value in Relationship. 'Respect' - as the Right Evaluation. Values in Human-to-Human Relationship. Understanding Harmony in the Society. Vision for the Universal Human Order.

units.title: Harmony in the Nature
units.topics: Understanding Harmony in the Nature, Interconnectedness, self-regulation and Mutual Fulfilment among the Four Orders of Nature, Realizing Existence as Coexistence at All Levels, The Holistic Perception of Harmony in Existence, Professional Ethics in the light of Right Understanding, Strategies for Transition towards Value-based Life and Profession.

units.title: Properties of Fluids and Fluid Statics
units.topics: Properties of fluids: fluid, fluid mechanics, ideal fluids, real fluids, mass density, specific weight, specific volume, specific gravity, viscosity - dynamic and kinematic, classification of fluids (rheological diagram), surface tension, capillarity, vapour pressure, compressibility and elasticity. Fluid statics: pressure, Pascal's law, hydrostatic law, atmospheric, absolute, gauge and negative pressure, pressure measuring devices. Total pressure, center of pressure. Pressure on horizontal, vertical, inclined and curved surfaces.

units.title: Fluid Kinematics
units.topics: Eulerian and Lagrangian approach, velocity and acceleration in Cartesian co-ordinates, Classification of flows, streamline, stream tube, path line, streak line, control volume. Equation of continuity for 3-D flow, components of rotation, velocity potential, stream function, flow net.

units.title: Fluid Dynamics
units.topics: Forces acting on fluid mass in motion, Euler's equation of motion along a streamline and integration to get Bernoulli's equation and its limitations, Modified Bernoulli's equation, HGL and TEL, Application of Bernoulli's equation: Venturimeter, Orifice meter, Rota-meter and Pitot tube.

units.title: Flow Through Pipes
units.topics: Characteristics of laminar flow, Hagen Poiseuille equation, Hazen-Williams formula. Characteristics of turbulent flow, Darcy-Weisbach Equation, Moody's diagram, Major and minor losses of energy in pipes, flow through pipes in simple and compound pipe, pipes in series, parallel, Dupit's equation, Introduction to pipe network and design: Hardy cross method.

units.title: Open Channel Flow
units.topics: Classification of channels, channel flows and geometric elements, Velocity distribution in open channel flow and hydraulic jump. Uniform flow: Chezy's and Manning's formulae, Factors affecting Manning's roughness coefficient. Most efficient channel sections: rectangular, trapezoidal. Depth-Energy Relationships: Specific energy and Specific force diagram, Depth discharge Diagram, Critical depth, Conditions for critical flow, Froude's number, flow classification, Introduction to channel transition.

units.title: Fundamentals of Structure and Analysis of Redundant Beams
units.topics: Types and classification of structures based on structural forms, concept of indeterminacy: static and kinematic indeterminacy. Analysis of propped cantilever, fixed beam and continuous beams within determinacy up to second degree by consistent deformation method.

units.title: Analysis of Redundant Frames
units.topics: Analysis of redundant trusses by unit load method for external loading, lack of fit, sinking of support and temperature changes (indeterminacy up to second degree). Approximate methods of analysis of upto two-storied two-bay, 2-D rigid jointed frames by Cantilever and Portal method.

units.title: Slope-Deflection Method
units.topics: Slope-deflection equations, equilibrium equation, application to beams with and without joint translation and rotation, yielding of support, application to non-sway rigid jointed rectangular portal frames, shear force and bending moment diagram. Sway analysis of rigid jointed portal frames (up to three unknowns).

units.title: Moment Distribution Method
units.topics: Stiffness factor, carry over factor, distribution factor, application of moment distribution method to beams with and without joint translation and yielding of support. Application to non-sway rigid jointed rectangular portal frames, shear force and bending moment diagram. Sway analysis of rigid jointed portal frames (up to three unknowns).

units.title: Stiffness Method
units.topics: Fundamental concepts of matrix methods: flexibility and stiffness. Stiffness method of analysis: Structure approach & Member approach. Application to beams by structure approach (up to three unknowns). Application to rigid jointed portal frames by structure approach (up to three unknowns).

units.title: Fundamentals of Concrete Technology
units.topics: Introduction to concrete and its importance. Cement: Raw materials, manufacturing, composition, types, hydration, and properties. Aggregates: Types, properties, quality control, and recycled aggregates. Water: Quality requirements and its role. Admixtures: Types, functions, and modern admixtures. Fibers: Types, and functions.

units.title: Properties of Fresh and Hardened Concrete
units.topics: Workability and factors affecting workability. Tests on fresh concrete: Slump, compaction factor, Vee-Bee, flow table test. Setting time and bleeding of concrete. Strength development: Compressive, tensile, flexural strength. Factors affecting strength and durability. Microstructure of hardened concrete. Permeability. Non-destructive testing: Rebound hammer, ultrasonic pulse velocity, penetration resistance, pull-out test.

units.title: Concrete Mix Design
units.topics: Principles of mix design. Design mix, nominal mix, methods of concrete mix design. Batching, mixing, transportation, placement, compaction, curing. IS 10262 method of concrete mix design. Case studies of concrete failure due to improper mix design. Introduction and mix design of High Strength Concrete, Ultra High Performance concrete (UHPC).

units.title: Durability and Sustainability of Concrete
units.topics: Importance of durability. Causes and mechanisms of deterioration: Sulphate attack, chloride ingress, alkali-silica reaction. Corrosion of reinforcement: Mechanism and prevention. Permeability, porosity, and water absorption. Sustainable concrete: Use of recycled aggregates, industrial by-products, and green cements. Introduction to life cycle analysis of concrete.

units.title: Advanced and Special Concretes
units.topics: High performance concrete, self-compacting concrete, fiber reinforced concrete. Lightweight concrete, pervious concrete, high density concrete. 3D printed concrete and digital fabrication techniques. Smart concrete: Self-healing concrete, sensor embedded concrete. Nano technology in concrete. Green concrete. Composite concrete.

units.title: Rock Science
units.topics: Introduction to Applied Engineering Geology. Mineral Definition, types of minerals, Industrial minerals (Computer, Medicine, Electronics Industry). Petrology: Rocks Definition, Types, Importance, Application in Civil Industry and other industries. Economic zones in India.

units.title: Remote Sensing and GIS, Hydrogeology
units.topics: Remote Sensing: Concepts, platforms, types of Sensors, Fundamentals of EMR, Resolutions, Visual Interpretation, Applications. GIS: Introduction, Definition, Components, GIS data types, Applications in Engineering, Smart Cities planning. Hydrogeology: Fundamentals, Groundwater, Water table, depth zones, Hydrogeological properties, Aquifers and its types, Artificial recharge of groundwater, Conservation of groundwater, Watershed development and management, Indian Knowledge System for Hydrology.

units.title: Structural Geology and Preliminary Geological Exploration
units.topics: Structural Geology: Plate tectonics, Mountain building activity, Outcrop, dip and strike, unconformity and overlap. Major geological structures: faults, folds, joints and their types, Recognition and significance in civil engineering. Preliminary Geological Exploration: reconnaissance survey, surface and subsurface investigations: Direct methods: test & trial pits, pilot trenches, drilling. Indirect methods: Resistivity, seismic survey.

units.title: Preliminary Geological Investigation of Dam Tunnel and Highways
units.topics: Dams: Types and foundation requirement, geological and geotechnical factors for dam site selection, seepage control and grout curtain, Reservoir-induced seismicity. Tunnel: Geological and geotechnical investigations for tunnels, Rock mass classification (RMR, Q-system), Methods of tunnelling: Drill & blast, TBM, and NATM, Geological hazards in tunnelling. Highways: Geotechnical considerations in highway alignment, Slope stability and landslide mitigation, Geological mapping and remote sensing, Use of geo-synthetics.

units.title: Geohazards
units.topics: Definition, and types. Causes, Effects, Precautions and case studies: Floods, Earthquakes, Landslides.

subjects.title: Vocational Skill Course: Applications of Python

units.title: Introduction to Project Management
units.topics: Importance, objectives & functions of management, principles of management, categories of project, project failure, project life cycle concept and cost components, PMBOK different domain areas, project management institute and certified project management professionals (PMP), Importance of organizational structure in management.

units.title: Project Planning and Scheduling
units.topics: WBS, Gantt / Bar chart & its limitations, network planning, network analysis, CPM - Activity on Arrow (AOA), critical path and type of floats, precedence network analysis (AON), types of Precedence Relationship, PERT Analysis.

units.title: Project Resources and Site Planning
units.topics: Objectives of materials management, material procurement procedures, record keeping: use of excel sheets, ERP software, inventory control: ABC analysis, EOQ technique, introduction to equipment management: productivity studies, site layout and planning, safety norms - measures and precautions on site, implementation of safety programs.

units.title: Project Monitoring, Control and Appraisal
units.topics: Resource allocation: resource smoothening and leveling, network crashing - time-cost relationship, resource optimization, project monitoring: methods, updating and earned value analysis, introduction to use of project management software: MS project / Primavera. Types of appraisals: political, social, environmental, technical, financial and economical, project feasibility report and DPR, role of project management consultants.

units.title: Fundamentals of Environmental Studies and Natural Resources
units.topics: Introduction to Environmental Studies: Multidisciplinary nature, components of the environment (atmosphere, hydrosphere, lithosphere, biosphere), scope and importance, sustainability and sustainable development. Ecosystems: Structure and function, energy flow (food chains, food webs, ecological succession), case studies. Natural Resources: Land use change, land degradation, soil erosion, desertification; deforestation; water use and over-exploitation, floods, droughts; renewable and non-renewable energy, alternate sources, energy needs.

units.title: Biodiversity and its Conservation
units.topics: Levels of Biodiversity: Genetic, species, and ecosystem diversity; biogeographic zones of India; global biodiversity hotspots; India as a mega-biodiversity nation. Biodiversity in India: Endangered and endemic species; threats to biodiversity. Conservation and Value of Biodiversity: In-situ and ex-situ conservation methods; biodiversity and ecosystem services: ecological, economic, social, ethical, aesthetic, and informational value.

units.title: Environmental Pollution and Climate Issues
units.topics: Types, causes, effects, and control of pollution: air, water, soil, chemical, noise. Nuclear hazards and health risks. Solid waste management. Climate change, global warming, ozone depletion, acid rain. Environmental laws: Environment Protection Act, Air and Water Acts, Wildlife Protection Act, Forest Conservation Act. International agreements: Montreal Protocol, Kyoto Protocol, CBD, CWC. Nature reserves, tribal rights, human-wildlife conflicts.

units.title: Human and Social Aspects of Environment
units.topics: Human population growth and its impact on environment and health, Carbon footprint and environmental ethics, Resettlement and rehabilitation of displaced populations, Disaster management: floods, earthquakes, cyclones, landslides, Environmental movements: Chipko, Silent Valley, Bishnois of Rajasthan, Role of religions and cultures in conservation, Environmental communication and public awareness.

files.title: TE Civil Syllabus with Honors
files.programme: Third Year Engineering (Civil Engineering) with Honors

units.title: Design philosophy & Tension Members
units.topics: Design Philosophy: Types of steel structures & applications, Steel properties, grades, rolled sections, IS Codes overview (IS 800, IS 875, IS 808), Limit State Design philosophy, Load combinations, factor of safety. Introduction to pre - engineered buildings & cold form light gauge section: including concept, components, and advantages. Concept of sustainability in steel construction, including recyclability, resource efficiency, and reduced environmental impact over the structure lifecycle Design of Tension Members: Tension member: various cross sections such as solid threaded rod, cable and angle sections limit strength due to yielding, rupture and block shear, design of tension me mbers of a truss using single and double angle sections and design of connection.

units.title: Design of Compression Members and Columns
units.topics: Buckling classification, buckling curves, classification of cross, effective length for compression members an d columns, design compressive stress, design of compression member of trusses using single and double angle section and design of connections. Design of axially loaded column using rolled steel section, design of built-up column, lacing and battening and its connections.

units.title: Design of Flexural Members
units.topics: Design bending strength, laterally restrained and unrestrained beams, design of laterally restrained beams using single rolled steel section with and without flange plate, curtailment of flang e plates, low and high shear, check for web buckling, web crippling and deflection. Design of laterally unrestrained beams using single rolled steel section, check for and deflection, design of purlin.

units.title: Eccentric Loaded Columns & Column Bases
units.topics: Design of eccentrically loaded column providing uniaxial and biaxial bending for section strength & Member strength. Design of column bases: slab base, gusseted base and moment resistant base for axial load, uni-axial and bi-axial bending.

units.title: Design of plate girder & gantry girder
units.topics: Design of Welded Plate Girder: Concept of plate girder, components of welded plate girder, intermittent weld, design of cross section, curtailment of flange plates, end bearing, load bearing, and intermedia te stiffeners, design of connection between flange & web plate and web plate & stiffeners, check for shear buckling of web, shear capacity of end panel and serviceability condition. Design of gantry girder: selection and design of cross section, check for moment capacity, buckling resistance, bi -axial bending, serviceability and fatigue strength. LEARNING RESOURCES

units.title: Introduction and Index Properties
units.topics: Introduction to Geotechnical Engineering and its applications to Civil Engineering. Types of soil structure, major soil deposits of India, Clay Mineralogy and Behavior. Field identification of soils. Introduction to soil exploration: objective and purpose. methods of Investigation: trial pits, borings, depth & number of exploration holes, core recovery, RQD, core log, geophysical methods: seismic refraction and electrical resistivity method) Three phase soil system: weight – volume relationships, Index properties of soil: Methods of determination and their significance. IS and Unified Soil classification systems, AASHTO, Triangular soil classification.

units.title: Permeability and Earth Pressure
units.topics: Permeability and Earth Pressure: Soil water, permeability definition and necessity of its study, Darcy’s law, factors affecting permeability. Permeability of stratified soil deposits. Seepage and Seepage Pressure, quick sand phenomenon, critical hydraulic gradient, General flow equation for 2-D flow Laplace equation. Earth Pressure – Introduction, Rankine’s state of Plastic Eq uilibrium in soils- Active and Passive states due to wall movement, Earth Pressure at rest. Rankine’s Theory: Earth pressure on Retaining wall due to submerged backfill.

units.title: Compaction and Stress Distribution
units.topics: Compaction – Introduction, Comparison between compaction and consolidation. Compaction tests- Standard Proctor test, Modified Proctor test. Zero air void line. Factors affecting compaction. Effect of compaction on soil properties. Field compaction methods and compaction equipment for d ifferent types of soil, Placement water content, Field compaction control- use of compaction test result. Proctor needle in field compaction control. Stress Distribution in Soils – Geostatic stress, Boussinesq’s theory with assumptions for point load and circular load (with numerical), Pressure Distribution diagram on a horizontal and vertical plane, Pressure bulb and its significance. Westergaard’s theory, equivalent point load method. Approximate stress distribution method.

units.title: Shear Strength of Soil
units.topics: Introduction – Shear strength an Engineering Property. Mohr’s stress circle, Mohr - Coulomb failure theory. The effective stress principle- Total stress, effective stress and neutral stress / pore water pressure. Peak and Residual shear strength, factors affecting shear strength. Stress-strain behaviour of sands and clays. Measurement of Shear Strength – Direct Shear test, Triaxial Compression test, Unconfined Compression test, Vane Shear test. Their suitability for different types of soils, adv antages and disadvantages. Different drainage conditions for shear tests. Sensitivity and thixotropi of cohesive soils. Field tests- SPT, N value correction and significance, DCPT, SCPT and introduction of advanced testing techniques like pressure meter te st, borelog, contents of sample soil investigation report.

units.title: Bearing Capacity
units.topics: Basic definitions, modes of shear failure, bearing capacity analysis- Terzaghi’s, and IS code method - rectangular and circular footings, bearing capacity evalu ation: plate load test and SPT, Housel’s perimeter shear concept, bearing capacity of layered soil, effect of water table on bearing capacity, effect of eccentricity, presumptive bearing capacity. LEARNING RESOURCES

units.title: Overview of Construction Management, Scheduling and Work Study
units.topics: Role of construction industry in economic development , Stakeholders in construction projects, Construction management: necessit y, Scope and applications, project management consultants: role, types, selection and appointment process, Construction project scheduling: definition, objectives factors affecting scheduling, line of balance technique, Work study (time and motion study): definition, objectives, process of method study, symbols, multiple activity charts, two handed process chart, string diagram.

units.title: Labour Laws and Financial Aspects of Construction Project
units.topics: Need and importance of labour laws, study of important labour laws associated with construction sector: workman’s compensation act 1923, building and other construction workers act 1996, child labour act, interstate migrant workers act, the minimum wages act 1948. Brief introduction to the Labour Codes—Code on Wages, 2019 and Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020. Capital investments: importance and difficulties, Sources of finance, working capital requirements, project cash flow projections and statements, project balance sheet, profit loss account statements.

units.title: Risk Management and Value Engineering
units.topics: Risk Management: introduction, principles, steps in risk management, risk in construction, origin, use of mathematical models: sensitivity analysis, break even analysis, simulation analysis (examples), decision tree analysis, risk identification, mitigation of project risks, role of insurance in risk management and case study on risk management. Value Engineering: meaning of value, types of value, value analysis, value e ngineering and its application, energy cost escalation and its impact on infrastructure project.

units.title: Material Management and AI Techniques in Civil Engineering
units.topics: Material: introduction, need, objectives, functions and scope of material management, integrated concept of material management, material management organization, various phases of material flow system, application of ech phase, role of material manager, role of material management in construction management and its linkage with oth er functional areas, stores management and control, concept of logistics and supply chain management. Introduction to artificial intelligence technique, basic terminologies and applications in civil engineering: artificial neural network, fuzzy logic and g enetic algorithm, Emerging technologies: IoT in construction, Drones for monitoring, Digital twins (introductory concept)

units.title: Human Resource Management and BIM Applications in Construction
units.topics: Human resource: introduction, nature and scope of human resource management, human resource in construction sector, staffing policy and patterns, human resource management process, human resource development process, recruitment & selection, performance evaluation and appraisal, training & development, s uccession planning, compensation and benefits, career planning, human resources information systems, HR data and analytics, role of ERP in human resource management and human resource information system. BIM (Building Information Modelling): Introduction t o BIM concepts and benefits, BIM levels and LOD (Level of Development), Applications of BIM in project planning and coordination, Overview of BIM software tools LEARNING RESOURCES

units.title: Supplementary Cementitious Materials and Advanced Cement Systems
units.topics: Fly ash, GGBS, silica fume, metakaolin, rice husk ash and other pozzolanic materials. Hydration and microstructure of cementitious systems. Interfacial transition zone. Chemical admixtures: Superplasticizers, shrinkage reducing admixtures, corrosion inhibiting admixtures. Rheology of concrete. Nano materials in concrete: Nano silica, ca rbon nanotubes, graphene oxide.

units.title: Performance-Based Concrete and Advanced Mix Design
units.topics: Performance requirements for concrete. Limitations of nominal and conventional mix design methods. Performance- based mix proportioning. Packing density a pproach. Mix design and properties of High Strength Concrete (HSC), High Performance Concrete (HPC), Self-Compacting Concrete (SCC), Fiber Reinforced Concrete (FRC), and Ultra High-Performance Concrete (UHPC). Quality control and statistical concepts in concrete production.

units.title: Durability and Service Life of Concrete
units.topics: Durability concepts and service life approach. Transport mechanisms in concrete. Chloride ingress, carbonation, sulphate attack, alkali aggregate reaction. Corrosion of reinfor cement: Mechanism, initiation and propagation. Durability provisions in IS codes and international practices. Durability assessment and service life prediction of reinforced concrete structures. Concrete for marine and aggressive environments.

units.title: Advanced Concrete Construction and Evaluation Techniques

Precast and prestressed concrete production techniques. 3D printed concrete and digital fabricati on.
